description: Concentrated high-performing professional alkaline detergent suitable for removing organic dirt and to undertake a deep clean of surfaces. It is also effective as a wax remover for water-based and metal-flake waxes
whereToUse: It is an excellent product suitable for cleaning and removing colored stains, oil, organic dirt and traffic marks from dirty surfaces such as:
porcelain, ceramic, glass, unpolished natural stone, concrete, terracotta, terrazzo.
When used undiluted, it removes stains from porcelain tiles.

Thanks to its effective cleaning and degreasing action, it is ideal for the preparation of existing ceramic and stone material before installing "tile-on-tile", with a cementitious adhesive or before applying a cementitious levelling compound to ensure full adhesion and to avoid detachments.
It is ideal for restoring surfaces, including removing previous water-based and metallic wax treatments.
notFor: Never use UltraCare HD Cleaner on waxed surfaces, unless to remove their treatment, or surfaces treated with products that are not resistant to wax-removing detergents.
Do not use on wood or polished stone.
Undertake a test when using on PVC, rubber and linoleum to check their compatibility with the colour and surface finish.

consumption.basis: one litre of product diluted at a 1:20 ratio with water
consumption.quote: With one litre of UltraCare HD Cleaner diluted at a 1:20 ratio with water, you can clean approximately 200 m2 of surface.

consumption.basis: diluted at a 1:5 ratio with water (the sentence does not restate the quantity of product; it follows the 'one litre' sentence)
consumption.quote: Diluted at a 1:5 ratio with water coverage is approximately 30 m2 of surface area.

mixing: Use UltraCare HD Cleaner diluted with water at a 1:10 to 1:20 ratio for deep cleaning of surfaces.
packaging: UltraCare HD Cleaner is available in 1 and 5 litre jerrycans.
storage: UltraCare HD Cleaner stored in the original packaging has a storage time of 3 years.
notes: 1) The sheet has no WHERE TO USE heading; whereToUse items are taken verbatim from the PRODUCT INFORMATION section, which is where the sheet lists surfaces and uses. 2) The 1:5 coverage sentence ('approximately 30 m2') does not say per how much product; it directly follows the 'With one litre...' sentence, so per litre is implied but not stated. The two figures are not proportional to dilution (1:20 gives 200 m2, 1:5 gives 30 m2), so do not interpolate between them. The sheet adds: 'Consumption depends on dilution, the degree and type of dirt, and the surface to be treated.' No coverage is given for undiluted use or for 1:10. 3) 'mixing' holds only the deep-cleaning dilution. The sheet gives three use strengths: undiluted (stains on porcelain tiles, left 'until completely dry (about one hour at +23°C and 50% relative humidity)'), 1:10 to 1:20 (deep cleaning), and 1:5 (stubborn dirt or grease, and wax removal). 4) The table row 'Waiting time before rinsing: 5 minutes' differs from the body text, which says to leave the diluted solution 'to act for 5-10 minutes' and the undiluted product about one hour. 5) The sheet writes 'm2' (not m²) in the consumption sentences; kept as printed. 6) No standards or classifications are stated. The sheet does not state whether dilution ratios are product:water by volume. 7) The printed quotation marks around tile-on-tile are typographic in the sheet; written here as straight quotes.
